extracted.intended_audience: examiners at International Searching Authorities and patent office staff responsible for PCT international search and related procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for International Searching Authority examiners on planning, conducting, recording and reporting the PCT international search (including selection of citations, handling of documentary and internet resources, treatment of doubtful or excluded subject matter, and procedures for supplementary searches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections must not introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correction requested or made must not introduce new matter into the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant does not make requested corrections within the time limit, the examiner proceeds with search/examination covering subject matter to which the claims might reasonably be expected to be directed after correction. If corrections are not made, the International Bureau may omit the noted matter from publication (Article 21(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of rectifications and Rule 9.1 corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on rectification under Rule 91.1 (Form PCT/ISA/217) or corrections to comply with Rule 9.1 must be transmitted to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections aimed at complying with Rule 9.1 must also be transmitted to the receiving Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information meeting Rule 48.2(l) — no obligation to check
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority (ISA) is not obliged to check whether the international application or other documents contain information meeting the criteria of Rule 48.2(l).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ISA notes information that appears to meet Rule 48.2(l) criteria, it may suggest the applicant request the International Bureau to omit the information from international publication using Form PCT/ISA/215.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to file when IB omits information
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the International Bureau has notified the ISA that it has omitted information from international publication or public file access, the ISA must not provide access to that omitted information except to the applicant or a person authorized by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA may provide access to any replacement sheet(s) received from the International Bureau accompanying Form PCT/IB/385.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine cited documents relevant to invention understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the international application should be examined if cited as the starting point of the invention, as showing the state of the art, as alternative solutions, or when necessary for correct understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations that clearly relate only to details not directly relevant to the claimed invention may be disregarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cited but inaccessible documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application cites a document that is not published or otherwise not accessible and that document appears essential to understanding the invention so that a meaningful search cannot be done without it, the ISA may postpone the search and request a copy from the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no copy is received, the ISA should first attempt the search and then, if necessary, indicate that no meaningful search could be carried out in total or that the search needed to be restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and title definitive by completion of ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should consider the abstract (and title and figure to be published with the abstract) and determine its definitive contents no later than the completion of the international search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under certain circumstances the examiner will have to establish the abstract/title/select the figure for publication; the abstract is established in the language of publication or in a transmitted translation if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification according to IPC
rubrics_metrics.description: After considering the abstract, the examiner classifies the international application according to at least the International Patent Classification (IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 7 for classification guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication prior to search — prepare classification/abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: If publication of the international application is due before the international search has been established, the examiner must, upon request by the International Bureau, establish the classification and examine the abstract/title/selected figure for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination for publication only ensures the abstract relates to the application and does not conflict with title or classification; if applicant provided none, the examiner should do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search statement defining subject of search
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be desirable for the examiner to prepare a written search statement defining the subject of the search as precisely as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may serve but may need generalization to cover all aspects/embodiments. Consider exclusions from international search and lack of unity; any restrictions should be indicated in the international search report; if no search is made, issue a declaration under Article 17(2)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims should be construed considering claim types
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be construed and searched with particular regard to the various types and forms of claims used, such as two-part claims and product-by-process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs 15.21 to 15.33 for details on claim types and their treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of search — consult PCT minimum documentation and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA endeavors to discover as much relevant prior art as its facilities permit and consults the appropriate minimum documentation specified in Rule 34 and relevant databases or search resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider databases/resources listed in the Search Guidance IPDL and other specialized systems, abstracting journals, and online databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive principle with economy judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle consult all documents within the field of search irrespective of language, age, or document type, but exercise judgment to omit file segments or databases where the likelihood of finding relevant documents is very small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, omit documents from periods before the technology began to develop; consult only one patent-family member unless substantial content differences or publication timing justify otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of classification places including analogous fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification places to be included in the international search should be selected in all directly relevant fields and, if necessary, in analogous fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the IPC, limit selection of analogous fields to (i) higher subdivisions allowing searching by abstraction when technically justified, and (ii) parallel subdivisions, being mindful they may be increasingly unrelated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select search strategies by expert judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Often various search strategies are possible; the examiner should exercise judgment and experience to select the most appropriate strategies and the order in which to consult classification places, databases and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to the main technical field and to resources/strategies with the highest probability of finding relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogous fields — basis for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Fields to be regarded as analogous are considered in light of the necessary function or use of the claimed invention, not only specific functions in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider (i) fields where same/similar structure is expected to be used in different work/use; (ii) fields to which a generic concept of claimed features pertains; (iii) art within the inventor’s endeavor reasonably pertinent to the problem involved; (iv) fields relevant to the function or utility inherent in claimed subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to extend search to unmentioned fields — guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to extend the international search to fields not mentioned in the application is left to examiner judgment and the examiner should not imagine all possible applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overriding principle: extend search only where it is possible that a reasonable objection of lack of inventive step could be established on the basis of what is likely to be found in those fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus of search — novelty, inventive step and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner carries out the search directing attention to prior art likely to have bearing on novelty or inventive step, and is encouraged to cite prior art useful for determining sufficiency of description across the whole field claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also note documents that may put doubt on validity of priority, aid understanding, or illustrate background, but do not spend time searching for these unless special reason exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentrate on high-probability resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate search efforts on resources and strategies in which the probability of finding highly relevant documents is greatest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When intending to cite prior art for sufficiency, identify all documents regardless of publication dates which are highly relevant to novelty, inventive step, adequacy of support and industrial applicability; consider search results already obtained before deciding to extend the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search patent literature first; include non-patent literature when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically conduct a search of patent literature first; in certain areas a search of non-patent literature may be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If little or no relevant patent prior art is located, consider broadening to databases containing non-patent literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: No special search for demonstrably well-known features
rubrics_metrics.description: No special search should be made for features that are instantly and unquestionably demonstrable as being well known such that documentary evidence seems unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably cite a handbook or other document showing the feature is generally known if practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of Internet searching
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the Internet as a search tool, treat all web sites as non-secure unless a commercial arrangement and secure connection exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secure connections where available; exercise extreme caution because Internet queries may be recorded and reveal details before publication. If no secure connection exists, searches may use generalized search terms representing combinations of features already known to exist in the state of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no documents found — cite technological background
rubrics_metrics.description: If no documents of more relevant nature for assessing novelty and inventive step are available, consider citing documents most relevant to the technological background noted during the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special search effort is generally required for this purpose; in exceptional cases an international search may be completed without any relevant document having been found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping the search — when to end
rubrics_metrics.description: Use judgment to end the search when the probability of discovering further relevant prior art becomes very low in relation to the effort needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stop also when documents found clearly demonstrate lack of novelty in the entire subject matter to which the claims are directed (with exceptions for well-known features). Do not stop if lack of novelty is demonstrated for only a limited number of claimed embodiments. Continue searching if outstanding issues about sufficiency, support, or industrial applicability could be clarified by additional prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording the search history
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the search history of the international search including classification identification of fields searched and, where useful, sufficient detail to allow national-stage examiners to interpret and rely upon the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of patent and non-patent literature searches, Internet searches (key words and query operators), actual search queries where practical, sequence alignments for sequence searches, chemical structure search basis, and database names. There is no requirement to include all details unless the ISA policy requires it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply PCT standards for novelty and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate prior art against the standards for novelty and inventive step as set out in Chapters 12 and 13 of the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the claimed invention meets those substantive requirements when selecting citations and forming conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discard documents because of doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not discard documents merely because of doubt as to exact date of publication, public availability, or exact contents of an oral disclosure/exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try to remove doubts and cite documents unless the date/public availability is clearly the same as or later than the filing date. Cite documents as category “L” where the date is not clearly established and indicate this in the search report; additional documents providing evidence in matters of doubt may be cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and verification of indicated publication dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Any indicated publication date in a document should be accepted as correct unless evidence shows otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an indicated date is insufficiently precise, endeavor to establish the exact date with sufficient precision (use stamped receipt dates or other references where helpful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special attention for excluded subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Give special attention when evaluating prior art for subject matter which may be excluded from the international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject matter is considered excluded in the ISA, assign the category symbol based on subject matter that might reasonably be expected to be claimed by amendment. Where other claims are directed to non-excluded subject matter, consider the non-excluded claims in the assessment; if non-excluded, assign category symbol based on claims appearing in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of citations — include most relevant and identify portions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the search, select documents to be cited in the international search report that always include the most relevant documents, which will be specially characterized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less relevant documents should be cited only when they concern aspects or details not found in already-selected documents. In doubt or borderline novelty/inventive step cases, readily make citations so applicant/designated Offices/International Preliminary Examining Authority can consider the matter more fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of third-party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the International Bureau transmits a third party observation in time to be taken into account, any prior art referred to in the observation should be considered for inclusion as if the examiner had found it, provided a copy or immediate availability is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the prior art listed in the observation only if considered relevant for inclusion in the international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid citing more documents than necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid increasing costs unnecessarily, the examiner should not cite more documents than necessary; when several documents are of equal relevance, the report should not normally cite more than one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple members of the same patent family are present, pay regard to language convenience and preferably cite (or note) documents in the language of the international application; consider designated Offices' translation needs and identify precisely the relevant part or passage of a cited document (page/paragraph/lines). Where an English family member is available, preferably indicate corresponding part of the English member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer documents in trusted/available files; justify unverified citations
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, select for citation only documents present in the search files of the ISA or to which access is readily available, so there is no doubt about contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under certain circumstances an unverified document may be cited if justified by identity of contents with another inspected document; both documents should then be mentioned. Assume contents of an abstract are contained in the original unless explicit indication otherwise; assume report of an oral disclosure matches the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify relevance before citing documents in unfamiliar languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Before citing documents in a language with which the examiner is not familiar, be satisfied that the document is relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use translation by a colleague, corresponding document/abstract in a familiar language, a drawing or chemical formula, or other means to verify relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and amend International Search Report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the international search report and the written opinion following completion of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If further relevant documents are discovered after ISR completion, they should be added up to the time of completion of technical preparations for publication by the IB. If a particularly relevant document is found within two years from the priority date, amend the ISR, mark it 'amended' and send copies to the applicant and the IB for transmission to designated Offices and IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling misdirected Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA, after transmittal of the ISR, receives by mistake amendments to the claims under Article 19, it should promptly transmit them to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the applicant accordingly as those amendments should have been filed with the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search is optional and supplemental
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary international search is an optional service (Rule 45bis) offered by Authorities that choose to provide it, intended as a supplement to the main international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It recognizes that no search can be completely exhaustive and is particularly relevant where the supplementary Authority has language specializations not available in the main ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limitations of supplementary search
rubrics_metrics.description: Details and scope of the service offered are decided by the Authority providing it and may be subject to limitations (e.g., subject matter, number of searches, number of claims searched).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope is defined in an annex to the agreement between the International Bureau and the Authority; details published in the PCT Applicant’s Guide Annex SISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting supplementary international search — timing and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: To request supplementary international search the applicant must submit a request to the International Bureau within 22 months from the priority date and pay the relevant fees within one month of submitting the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request is usually made after the applicant has seen the main ISR but that is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents transmitted to supplementary Authority upon valid request
rubrics_metrics.description: If request is valid and necessary items provided, the International Bureau transmits specified documents to the Authority designated for supplementary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents include: (i) supplementary search request; (ii) international application; (iii) sequence listings furnished; (iv) translations to be used as basis; and promptly after receipt: (v) international search report and written opinion; (vi) invitations to pay additional fees referred to in Article 17(3)(a); (vii) any protest under Rule 40.2(c) and decision by the ISA review body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of receipt by supplementary Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of the request for supplementary international search, the Authority promptly sends an acknowledgement of receipt of the copy of the international application to the applicant and to the International Bureau using Form PCT/SISA/506.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 519 and Rules 45bis.3(e), 45bis.5(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may reject request if excluded by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority finds carrying out the supplementary search is excluded by a limitation in the agreement (other than Article 17(2) limitations), it considers the request not to have been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authority notifies the applicant and the IB using Form PCT/SISA/507 and refunds the fee to the extent specified, using Form PCT/SISA/508 to notify repayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of supplementary international search — timing options
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search normally starts promptly on receipt of required documents, but may delay starting until it has received the international search report and written opinion or until the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 45bis.5(a) and Rule 45bis.4(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of main written opinion for supplementary Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written opinion of the main ISA is not in English or a language accepted by the supplementary Authority, the Authority may request the IB to provide a translation into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IB transmits such translation within two months of the date of receipt of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of request for supplementary international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the request at any time before transmittal of the supplementary international search report or declaration that no report will be established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal is effective on receipt within this time limit; processing should stop. There is no general obligation for the Authority to refund the fee at this stage (IB refunds if withdrawal before any documents sent); Authorities may offer refunds according to internal practice set out in the Agreement annex. If notice received directly from applicant, mark receipt date and promptly transmit copy to IB.
